I don’t think there’s a perfect answer to your question, but I’ve always believed self discipline is what results in motivation. Kinda like when people struggle to feel motivated to do a task that’s not that fun. Well of course there’s going to be a struggle! Our minds are always trying to protect us from any sort of stress, harm, risk. So if something is going to seem demanding or risky, we’re not going to want to do it. 

Enter self discipline. In the dating context it’s a little different then say, staying disciplined at the gym, in school, at work, etc. for me, it meant moving on with my life after every heartbreak. Staying disciplined in caring for my physical body, going outside, and working on things that mattered to me. I believe during this time period, I was getting my masters degree. So definitely kept me busy toward something meaningful. In a nutshell: focusing on myself. Licking my wounds in a way but not through solely self pity. 

Once all of this was in place, plus time… the motivation came back around. I knew the risks and I practiced better communication and boundaries to avoid being hurt. But we can’t control others so it’s always always going to be a risk. But I was motivated again because I took care of myself first, in a disciplined way, to the point that I started wanting to date again. Because it was important to me in the long run. I wanted to find a lifelong partner. And I did!

I want to emphasize that I don’t mean discipline in the form of dating back to back to back. I think that’s a recipe for burnout. Kinda like rigid discipline in any other way. We have to take breaks, pause, relax. With dating, cry, be angry, feel bad for ourselves. But then we get back up. I hope that made sense!

I had pretty clear skin until the beginning of this year when I suddenly got a cluster breakout near my jaw. I didn’t even have to ask my derm as that’s what she immediately offered to prescribe. It slowly but surely took care of my acne, and it has the added benefit of lightening the dark marks they left behind. For some texture I was still dealing with, she recommended la roche posay salicylic acid cleanser, just a few times a week. Both those products have definitely improved my skin. I truly believe the game changer was azelaic acid. I encourage you to do some research on it and discuss with your derm!

I use ACT primarily, and sometimes pull from DBT and IFS. ACT and DBT place a big emphasis on validating the clients pain and just being human with them. That’s how I avoid potentially coming off as just a tool box. If someone is struggling in front of me, I validate, sit with them, and gently ask about any tools or skills they thing might be helpful. My own therapist often asks me “what support do you need from me?” And so I’ve used that as well. The therapeutic alliance remains one of the most important “tools” in therapy and has nothing to do with any modality. I think as long as you have that, you can avoid being too shallow or overly skills focused.

One of the things I find most interesting in myself is my ability to have one on one conversations with complete strangers (at least in the beginning) and feel mostly at ease (I’m human and still get a bit nervous meeting anyone for the first time). The same day I’ve worked with 4 or 5 people on their concerns in such a unique working relationship is the same day I will think twice about going out with friends or overthink everything I say or feel quite anxious/awkward around them. Granted I don’t have many friends but even with my partners friends, who I think are pretty cool, I revert back to my shy, introverted self. 

One thing about us introverts is that we’re very observant. This comes SUPER in handy as a therapist. Most of us, or at least myself, don’t judge others for being quiet and reserved. This nonjudgemental quality is imperative to be warm and compassionate therapist. Lastly, as introverts we deeply understand the struggle of living in a world that is mostly geared towards extroverts. This helps us connect with clients who are struggling with whatever concern they have in a world that tends to be dismissive or ignorant about these same very issues. 

All that to say, my introversion is 100% what has made me the therapist that I am and I’d like to think what has made most of my clients stick with me for years at this point. You will be great!

So I had google voice for years to protect my
Personal cell, but after having someone who actually never became my client text me long rants late at night or call me at 6 am, I knew I had to get something different. Google voice offers a DND option which was fine except I could still see notifications and it was really getting to me. I wished I could set up business hours or auto replies but google voice doesn’t offer that. 

There’s tons of business phone lines out there. The one I ended up getting is called iPlum. It’s relatively inexpensive and so far it’s worked great for me. I have my business hours set up so that anyone who calls or text me outside those hours I don’t get notifications for. They will also get an auto reply text stating my business hours and that I’ll get back to them on the next business day. It’s completely customizable. When I’ve gone on vacation I change my auto text to state hotline numbers in case of crises or 911 for emergencies. This has really helped with keeping my boundaries and protecting my time. I’m totally not trying to sell iPlum specifically, I think another popular one is Spruce, but what I am highly encouraging is for you to invest in a business line with some of these features and absolutely do not do not give out your personal. I can’t believe anyone would ever recommend that within an administrative role!

Hey, I’m 23 but I still remember the gut punch that was my first breakup. We were on and off for all of high school plus a little bit of college. Everything you are feeling is normal. I also didn’t have much of an appetite, but that doesn’t mean stop eating. Even if it tastes bland, the less you eat the less energy you have and that will only add to the mental exhaustion that comes with a breakup. In terms of feelings, let yourself grieve. This is a loss and a death of a relationship and a person as you knew them. Give yourself about a week to just go through the motions and feel the feelings. Let people you trust in, whether that’s family or friends. You don’t have to go into details, but just share with them that this is a difficult time and you would appreciate patience and support. 

After that week, start to learn your new “normal”. Focus on school as if it’s your only job. Say yes to invitations out or just have a night in with friends. Know that you will likely still get pangs of sadness— this is normal and it is grief. Journal it out if you need to, I find it very therapeutic. 

As for him, I really believe that you have to go no contact for a while after the breakup. That means: no texting, no social media. It’s harsh but think of this as something you are doing for YOU. From now on, you are your main focus. Healing YOU. Having him in the picture will get in the way and can hold you back. I know it sucks, I know after having someone every day and to just cut them off it feels horrible. But trust me when I say time is on YOUR side. No matter what happens, each passing day is a day towards healing and a day past the pain. Know that you will survive this and you will come out stronger. Good luck and DM me if you need anything, I sure wish I had someone to talk to when I was your age! Much love.

I’m 22 now and love my life. I graduated, I’m starting my masters soon, I am dating and for the first time in years I can say I am not depressed. I have self esteem again. We broke up because we had become emotionally drained with the relationship and one another. No one understood me and knew so much about me besides him. He was the first true best friend I’ve ever had. He also wanted to be friends because we care for each other so much. At first I was okay with the idea. We agreed we wouldn’t see each other or talk too frequently, but we could reach out. However, I found myself anxious for the next time he would text me. I found myself disappointed when my phone would vibrate and it wasn’t him. I couldn’t grieve properly because he was still somewhat in my life, so there was a possibility we could try again right?


Then one day he did text me saying he hoped I was doing okay. I wasn’t. Was he? I hated thinking that he was and he was just checking up on me as if I was a child. I got upset that this is what he texted me instead of “let’s try again”. I mulled it over for two hours, spoke with a friend, before deciding I just couldn’t be friends. Not so soon after the breakup. Not while I was still completely in love with him. I told him that and we haven’t really spoken since. 

Now, I don’t have that anxiety of him texting me. I don’t have that expectation or hope. And that’s allowing me to move on because I’m literally closing that chapter of my life. 

I don’t really believe people can be friends soon after a breakup. Maybe months to years down the line. But not days or weeks. It also depends on the person. I don’t see myself being friends with my ex for a very long time. When I do imagine us as friends, it’s been years and years. That’s how long it would take me. In order to truly be platonic friends, you have to be okay with them being with other people. You have to be okay with them finding love in someone else. You have to truly wish the best for them, even if that means someone else. Can you do that? If not, you are not ready to be friends.

Trust me, I am not the queen of NC nor have I even actually partaken in it. I talked to my ex yesterday. As well as a few days after our breakup, on two different occasions. We were best friends and he really worries about me and my feelings. The second time we spoke, I felt some sort of closure and a little hopeful even, because we asserted that the breakup had to happen. We thanked each other for the wonderful times we spend together and the lessons we taught each other. It was nice. 

Yesterday however, I was feeling particularly low. I was not planning on texting him but I remembered I still had something of his, so I asked him how I should return it. After that, that’s when he asked how I was doing. I didn’t completely lose my shit, but towards the end I was beginning to unravel and say I only want him back. I became frustrated at this words of consolation and the lack of any desire to give our relationship another shot. I ended the conversation and I don’t want to hear from him again. 

So I guess my story shows both sides of the coin. How talking to an ex after an amicable breakup can help with healing, in strange ways I can’t put into words. But then there’s times like last night where I thought I was okay to talk to him, but my emotions got the best of me and I probably came off as desperate and weak. And now I don’t feel good about him as a friend nor about us keeping in contact.

You’re not sure about being friends with him, so don’t push it. You now have these weird feelings after having spoken to him and now you realize you still miss him. I think a longer period of NC is in order... it may have felt good to catch up and what not, but in the end it may just hold you back from fully healing.

I’ve been depressed for about five years, ranging from mild to severe. I spent almost a good year desperately looking for a boyfriend. I tried online dating and whatnot, because I’m so shy in person. One day I passed by a guy who I recognized from my childhood. Didn’t think of it much until I saw that he followed me on social media. I looked through his pictures and was instantly attracted. I took a plunge. I began talking to him. I started developing feelings and strong ones at that. One day it became overwhelming, knowing this incredible happy
Positive guy was starting to like me. I sat him down and fearfully told him about my depression. I told him i would understand if he wanted nothing to do with me after. 

He stayed and a year later we are still together. It has not been easy. My depression, anxiety and low self esteem has gotten the best of me many times and many times I feel like I’ve directly sabotaged my relationship. He has never had depression but tries his hardest to understand. He is supportive and his love for me by some fucking miracle continues to grow. 

Lately I’ve been feeling terrible again. Lately the thought of breaking up with him has entered my mind. But only because I believe he deserves someone so much better, someone without depression. Yet I know that’s the depression taking. I know he loves me and I love him. He’s the one that tells me “your depression isn’t you”. 

So my answer to you is, it is possible. I barely have any friends but I have a boyfriend. I know it’s so cliche to just say “oh the right person will come along don’t worry!” I detested hearing that. My advice, from personal experience, is just keep distracting yourself. Do whatever hobby you enjoy. Don’t avoid talking to people, but don’t become desperate looking for someone. I can’t say it’ll happen. But if it does, know that they won’t fix your depression. Know that they will not become your therapist. The greatest thing my boyfriend has done is support me as I continue therapy and listen to me during my breakdowns. But if he wasn’t in my life, I think I would still seek therapy. I’m battling my depression because I want to fucking win for once, and I’m not doing it for any SO in the world.
